clue.text: Gymnasium accommodates fashionable composer

indicators.note: a building that accommodates something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a palestra (palaestra) was a wrestling school or gymnasium in ancient Greece
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A gym is hosting a trendy composer, perhaps for a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The palestra (or palaestra) was the wrestling school of ancient Greece; 'accommodates' is the container signal, and 'fashionable' gives the familiar crossword IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina was the great Italian Renaissance writer of church music.

clue.text: Emotion stirred by Ford's fallen woman

definitions.text: Emotion stirred by Ford's fallen woman

parts.words: Emotion stirred by Ford's fallen woman
parts.note: John Ford's Jacobean tragedy is titled 'Tis ___ She's a Whore, naming the feeling its fallen heroine arouses

explanation.surface: A reader is moved by the plight of a ruined woman in a Ford play.
explanation.definitionFit: Compassion is the emotion named in the title of John Ford's play about Annabella, the fallen woman.

clue.text: He killed his father's killer, and so did his father's killer

definitions.text: He killed his father's killer, and so did his father's killer

parts.words: He killed his father's killer, and so did his father's killer
parts.note: in Hamlet, this son of Polonius kills Hamlet, who had slain Polonius; Hamlet in turn kills Claudius, his own father's murderer

explanation.surface: A riddle about a chain of revenge killings between two sons.
explanation.definitionFit: Polonius's son avenges his father by killing the prince, while that prince, Polonius's killer, avenges his own father on Claudius.

clue.text: Paras Land, a US version of Byron play

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworked form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paratroopers land in America in some military production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges PARAS LAND A US into the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Byron's verse tragedy of 1821 is named after the decadent last king of Assyria.

clue.text: Kipling's ghostly transportation

parts.note: Kipling wrote the supernatural tale The Phantom ___, about a haunting two-wheeled carriage pulled by a man

explanation.surface: A ghostly vehicle from a Kipling story.
explanation.definitionFit: A light hooded carriage pulled by a runner is the haunting vehicle of Kipling's early ghost story.

clue.text: Old woman's irritation in early play?

definitions.text: Old woman's irritation in early play?

parts.words: Old woman's irritation in early play?
parts.note: Gammer Gurton's ___ is an early English comedy; gammer means old woman, and the lost sewing tool also means an irritation or provocation

explanation.surface: An old woman is irked by something in an early drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Gammer is an old word for an elderly woman; the play is one of the first English comedies, c. 1550s.
explanation.definitionFit: The lost sewing implement in Gammer Gurton's play doubles as a word for annoyance, as in to goad someone.

clue.text: Musical family in Cordoba choir

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words Cordoba choir

explanation.surface: A family of musicians performs in a choir in Cordoba.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters spanning cordoBA CHoir.
explanation.definitionFit: The German dynasty of composers led by Johann Sebastian is the most famous musical clan.

clue.text: Absurd dramatist

parts.note: the Spanish playwright Fernando ___ is associated with the Theatre of the Absurd and his own Panic movement

explanation.surface: A ridiculous playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Absurd' reads as an insult, but refers to the Theatre of the Absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Fernando Arrabal, Spanish-born writer in France, is a leading figure of absurdist theatre.

clue.text: Edwardian novel featuring fate of Henry VIII's fifth wife?

definitions.meaning: E. M. Forster's 1910 novel about the Schlegels and Wilcoxes

definitions.text: fate of Henry VIII's fifth wife?
definitions.meaning: Catherine Howard, Henry's fifth queen, was beheaded, so her end was the Howard demise

explanation.surface: A novel of the Edwardian era that includes a Tudor queen's execution.
explanation.definitionFit: Forster's novel is named after a house; split as a possessive, it describes the death of Catherine Howard.

clue.text: Marine criminal for whom Stevenson shared responsibility

definitions.meaning: someone who lures ships onto rocks to plunder them
Robert Louis Stevenson co-wrote this 1892 novel with his stepson Lloyd Osbourne

explanation.surface: A seaside villain whose story Stevenson co-authored.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrecker causes shipwrecks for loot, and Stevenson and Osbourne jointly wrote a novel with that title.

clue.text: Banks defined this road

parts.note: Iain Banks wrote the novel The ___ Road, named after a Glasgow street

explanation.surface: Banks of earth line both sides of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like the verges of a road; it is the Scottish novelist Iain Banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Iain Banks's 1992 novel is The Crow Road, a Scottish euphemism for death.

clue.text: Cause of absolute disappearance of Christopher Hampton?

definitions.text: Cause of absolute disappearance of Christopher Hampton?

parts.words: Cause of absolute disappearance of Christopher Hampton?
parts.note: an event blotting out the sun entirely, and the title of Hampton's play about Verlaine and Rimbaud

explanation.surface: What made the playwright Christopher Hampton vanish entirely?
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon fully blocks the sun it disappears completely; Christopher Hampton's 1967 play bears that title.

clue.text: Colonnade fronting some temples of Athens

indicators.note: the fronts of these words, their opening letters, are taken

explanation.surface: A colonnade stands before several temples in Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fronting' takes the first letters of 'some temples of Athens'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa was a covered portico or colonnaded walk in ancient Greek cities.

clue.text: Local locale for Frank Harvey Jr.

definitions.text: Local locale for Frank Harvey Jr.

parts.words: Local locale for Frank Harvey Jr.
parts.note: a room in a British pub ('local'), and the setting and title of Frank Harvey Jr's 1939 stage thriller

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood pub room that a playwright made his setting.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for one's regular neighbourhood pub; the more comfortable lounge in it is this room.
explanation.definitionFit: The more refined room of an English public house gave its name to Frank Harvey's play set there.

clue.text: His activities might produce solid result

definitions.text: His activities might produce solid result

parts.words: His activities might produce solid result
parts.note: an image-breaker smashes statues, and the fragments ('clasts') of broken material form solid clastic rock

explanation.surface: Someone whose work yields a firm outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The image-breaker leaves broken pieces; clastic rock is solid stone built from such fragments, a playful link to the word's Greek root 'klastes', breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: One who smashes religious images, or attacks cherished beliefs, leaves broken fragments behind.

clue.text: Actors seemingly absent from work, defining 17 or 21

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast
someone absent from work is away

explanation.surface: Performers apparently off work describe the exiles of The Tempest.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 and 21 are Prospero and Miranda, marooned on the island in The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero and his daughter were set adrift and stranded on an island, making them shipwrecked exiles.

clue.text: Everything is following opening of toccata for early organist

indicators.note: following places these pieces after the opening letter
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A remark that all is well after a toccata begins on the organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' is the order signal: the opening letter of 'toccata' comes first, with the rest after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Tallis was a Tudor composer and organist of the Chapel Royal.

clue.text: He seems to thrive on nothing in exile, accompanied by 21

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: to thrive is to prosper
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An exile who seems to flourish with nothing, his daughter beside him.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is Miranda, who shares Prospero's island exile in The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: The deposed Duke of Milan lives banished on an island with his daughter Miranda.

clue.text: Martial arts figures from Japan, in jasper, ivory, or jade

indicators.note: from signals letters drawn out of the run of words Japan, in jasper

explanation.surface: Figurines of fighters from Japan carved in precious stones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' takes the letters spanning japaN IN JASper; 'ivory, or jade' is surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert Japanese agents trained in martial arts are figures of popular culture.

clue.text: "A man who has never looked upon —— has but a faint idea of a cataract" (Lord Macaulay)

definitions.text: "A man who has never looked upon —— has but a faint idea of a cataract" (Lord Macaulay)

parts.words: "A man who has never looked upon —— has but a faint idea of a cataract" (Lord Macaulay)
parts.note: Macaulay's quotation names the great falls on the US-Canada border as the supreme waterfall

explanation.surface: A quotation from Macaulay about the grandeur of a famous waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The great falls between Ontario and New York are the archetype of a cataract, an immense waterfall.

clue.text: Stern debut from ex-slave, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells you to go by how a word sounds

parts.note: a former slave is a freedman

explanation.surface: A severe first appearance from a former slave, reportedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Stern (1962) was Bruce Jay Friedman's first novel; 'Stern' poses as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruce Jay Friedman's first novel was Stern, so the novelist is the author behind that debut.

clue.text: She was expected by Belloc to recall some second-rate pub

definitions.text: She was expected by Belloc to recall some second-rate pub

parts.words: She was expected by Belloc to recall some second-rate pub
parts.note: Belloc's poem Tarantella opens 'Do you remember an Inn' addressed to a woman by name

explanation.surface: A woman Belloc hoped would remember a shabby inn.
explanation.definitionFit: Belloc's Tarantella asks a named woman to remember a Pyrenean inn with fleas and tar.

clue.text: Some total cover provides concealment in farce, opera buffa, etc

definitions.text: concealment in farce, opera buffa, etc

indicators.note: some means a portion of the words total cover is used

explanation.surface: Complete cover is where characters hide in a farce or comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes the letters spanning totAL COVEr.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess in a wall is the classic hiding place for lovers and eavesdroppers in stage comedy.

clue.text: Vestments belonging to Wildean doctor

definitions.meaning: sleeveless outer garments worn by a priest at Mass
the possessive of Canon Chasuble, D.D., the rector in The Importance of Being Earnest

explanation.surface: Clerical robes owned by a doctor in Wilde's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Liturgical robes share a name with Wilde's Dr Chasuble, so the possessive reads as his.

clue.text: It was intrumental in providing subject matter for Robertson Davies

definitions.text: It was intrumental in providing subject matter for Robertson Davies

parts.words: It was intrumental in providing subject matter for Robertson Davies
parts.note: Robertson Davies wrote The ___ of Orpheus; the thing named is literally a musical instrument

explanation.surface: Something helped give the novelist Robertson Davies his subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Orpheus's harp-like stringed instrument gave Davies the title of the last Cornish trilogy novel.

clue.text: Derisive reception heard for composer?

indicators.note: heard tells you to go by how a word sounds

parts.note: getting the bird means being booed or hissed

explanation.surface: A composer apparently hears himself jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bird' is British slang for a hostile, jeering reception.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd was the leading English composer of the Elizabethan age.

clue.text: Master of Bulwer-Lytton and Hood

parts.note: Eugene ___, the murderous schoolmaster, is the subject of Bulwer-Lytton's novel and Thomas Hood's poem

explanation.surface: Someone who taught two Victorian writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' seems to mean a teacher of the writers; it means a schoolmaster they both wrote about.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene Aram was an 18th-century schoolmaster hanged for murder, treated by both writers.

clue.text: Willing Bondswoman?

parts.note: M's devoted secretary in the James Bond stories, a woman willing to serve Bond, her name hinting at cash

explanation.surface: A slave woman who serves eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bondswoman' looks like a female serf; read as Bond's woman it is M's secretary in Ian Fleming's spy novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Moneypenny, M's secretary, is the woman forever pining for and helping James Bond.

clue.text: Bad driver, starts tearing off, accelerating dangerously

indicators.note: the starts of these words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A reckless motorist tears away, speeding hazardously.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Toad of The Wind in the Willows is literature's famous reckless motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Grahame's Toad of Toad Hall is notorious for crashing motor cars.

clue.text: "Nothing is so good as it seems ——' " (Silas Marner)

definitions.text: "Nothing is so good as it seems ——' " (Silas Marner)

parts.words: "Nothing is so good as it seems ——' " (Silas Marner)
parts.note: a line in George Eliot's novel about things seeming better in advance than they prove

explanation.surface: A quotation from George Eliot's Silas Marner about disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing adverb means in advance, before the event, completing Eliot's line.
